role: Patent Trial and Appeal Board panel of three Administrative Patent Judges issuing a Final Written Decision in an inter partes review (IPR), post-grant review (PGR), or covered-business-method (CBM) proceeding under 35 U.S.C. §§ 311-319 (IPR) / 321-329 (PGR/CBM); adjudicating patentability of challenged claims under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, and 112 by a preponderance-of-the-evidence standard
target: the patentability of contested patent claims under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, or 112, as challenged by the Petitioner and defended by the Patent Owner
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "Petitioner has shown by a preponderance of the evidence that a person of ordinary skill in the art would have been motivated to combine Smith's electrode configuration with Jones's protective coating with a reasonable expectation of success" citing KSR Int'l Co. v. Teleflex Inc., 550 U.S. 398, 406 (2007) is praise that evidences a 'KSR-motivation-to-combine-with-reasonable-expectation-of-success' norm; the phrase "Patent Owner's expert testimony lacks objective evidentiary support for the proposed claim-construction position, instead asserting bare attorney argument" is a complaint that evidences an 'expert-testimony-evidentiary-support / no-bare-attorney-argument' norm; the phrase "Gass discloses every limitation of claim 22 as set forth above and we are persuaded that Petitioner has shown by a preponderance of the evidence that claims 22 and 24-28 are anticipated by Gass" citing 35 U.S.C. § 102(b) is praise that evidences an 'anticipation-requires-every-limitation-in-single-prior-art-reference' norm; the phrase "under the broadest reasonable interpretation in light of the specification, 'integrally attached' means discrete parts physically joined together as a unit without each part losing its own separate identity" is an observation that evidences a 'BRI-claim-construction / specification-defines-claim-term' norm
polarity_hint:
PTAB Final Written Decisions are dominantly REASONING-MOVES rather than overt complaint or praise. The Board's voice is formal, first-person plural ('we hold', 'we are persuaded', 'we conclude', 'we credit', 'we find', 'we do not credit', 'we agree with Petitioner', 'we agree with Patent Owner'), with regular invocations of the Petitioner's burden and the Patent Owner's response. The Board systematically addresses each ground of unpatentability raised in the institution decision. Common norm-bearing moves include: (i) claim construction (since November 2018 the Phillips ordinary-and-customary-meaning standard applies; for older proceedings the broadest-reasonable-interpretation BRI standard applies) — usually `observation` with polarity `neutral`, or `praise`/`complaint` depending on whose proposed construction the Board adopts; (ii) § 102 anticipation — strict identity, requires every limitation in a single prior art reference; (iii) § 103 obviousness analyzed under the Graham v. John Deere four factors (scope and content of prior art, differences from claimed subject matter, level of ordinary skill, secondary considerations), with KSR-motivation-to-combine and reasonable-expectation-of-success required; (iv) POSITA (person of ordinary skill in the art) level determination, usually citing expert declarations; (v) expert-testimony evidentiary weight (the Board credits or does not credit expert opinions based on supporting documentation; bare attorney argument or conclusory expert testimony unsupported by evidence is unpersuasive — In re Magnum Oil Tools Int'l, Ltd., 829 F.3d 1364, Fed. Cir. 2016); (vi) § 112 written description / enablement / definiteness / new matter; (vii) § 101 patent-ineligibility (under Alice / Mayo two-step framework, especially for CBMs); (viii) secondary considerations (commercial success, long-felt need, copying, industry praise, failure of others, unexpected results — Graham factor 4), with NEXUS required to the patented invention; (ix) Petitioner's burden of proof by a preponderance of the evidence (35 U.S.C. § 316(e) for IPR); (x) real-party-in-interest under § 315(b) one-year statutory bar; (xi) analogous-art test (PersonalWeb Techs., LLC v. Apple, Inc., 848 F.3d 987, Fed. Cir. 2017) — same field of endeavor or reasonably pertinent to the inventor's problem; (xii) Patent Owner's swearing-behind / prior conception (35 U.S.C. § 102(g)). signal_type complaint is usually directed at the Petitioner for failing to meet the preponderance burden, at the Patent Owner for offering unpersuasive expert testimony, or at one party's proposed claim construction the Board rejects. signal_type praise is directed at the prevailing party for a well-supported argument, evidence, or expert declaration the Board credits. signal_type observation is the default for statements of the controlling standard, the disclosed content of a prior art reference, or the claim language. signal_type suggestion is for the Board's prescriptive doctrinal statements (typically a statement of the legal rule that future panels and parties must apply). Norm-bearing language is DENSE in PTAB FWDs — these are technical, methodical decisions with many doctrinal moves per page.

DATASET-SPECIFIC OVERRIDES (these REPLACE the generic constraints where they conflict):

(a) The input is a PTAB FINAL WRITTEN DECISION (often 30,000 to 200,000 chars). Aim for HIGH RECALL across the analysis: 10-30 passages per FWD is typical. Each passage should be a doctrinally-coherent unit (a claim-construction paragraph for a specific term, an anticipation analysis for a specific claim group over a specific reference, an obviousness combination analysis with KSR motivation, a § 112 written-description analysis, a secondary-considerations nexus analysis, etc.) rather than a sentence fragment. Bare procedural recitations (the caption, the panel of three Administrative Patent Judges, the 'Trials@uspto.gov' header, the case-number and patent-number banner, the procedural history block listing institution date and oral hearing date, the parties' counsel list, the exhibits list) emit ZERO signals.

(b) ATTRIBUTION RULE — signals must capture THE BOARD'S OWN reasoning, not the Petitioner's arguments, the Patent Owner's responses, or the experts' declarations as paraphrased. When the FWD says 'Petitioner argues X', 'Patent Owner responds Y', 'Dr. Greenspun testifies Z', 'PO Resp. 30 contends W' — that paraphrase is NOT itself a signal. The signal is the Board's own move ACCEPTING, REJECTING, or QUALIFYING that position. The clearest cues are the Board's voice: 'we hold', 'we conclude', 'we are persuaded', 'we are not persuaded', 'we credit', 'we do not credit', 'we agree with Petitioner', 'we agree with Patent Owner', 'we find', 'we determine', 'Petitioner has shown', 'Petitioner has not shown', 'we construe X to mean Y', 'we adopt Petitioner's proposed construction'. Also acceptable are unattributed declarative statements of the controlling standard ('A patent claim is obvious under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) if the differences…') which ARE the Board speaking in the doctrinal-exposition register.

(c) signal_type ENUM IS STRICTLY {complaint, praise, observation, suggestion}. (i) Statements of the controlling legal standard ('Under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a)…', 'The question of obviousness is resolved on the basis of underlying factual determinations including Graham v. John Deere Co., 383 U.S. 1, 17-18 (1966)…') and statements describing the disclosed content of a prior art reference ('Van Zandt discloses a comprehensive logistics support service…') are `observation` with polarity `neutral`. (ii) The Board rejecting Petitioner's argument, rejecting Patent Owner's proposed construction, finding expert testimony unsupported by evidence, or noting a Petitioner failure to meet the preponderance burden is `complaint` with polarity `negative` (the complaint is directed AT the unsuccessful party or its expert). (iii) The Board finding Petitioner has shown by a preponderance, adopting one party's claim construction, crediting expert testimony, or finding the prior art teaches a particular limitation is `praise` with polarity `positive`. (iv) Prescriptive statements of how doctrine SHOULD apply ('A patent claim is obvious if…', 'A POSITA must be defined as a hypothetical person…') are `suggestion`. Use `suggestion` for canonical-rule statements; use `observation` for case-specific applications.

(d) CITATION-INSIDE-PASSAGE: patent-law citations (e.g. 'KSR Int'l Co. v. Teleflex Inc., 550 U.S. 398, 406 (2007)', 'Graham v. John Deere Co., 383 U.S. 1, 17-18 (1966)', 'Phillips v. AWH Corp., 415 F.3d 1303 (Fed. Cir. 2005) (en banc)', 'In re Magnum Oil Tools Int'l, Ltd., 829 F.3d 1364 (Fed. Cir. 2016)', 'PersonalWeb Techs., LLC v. Apple, Inc., 848 F.3d 987 (Fed. Cir. 2017)') and exhibit / record citations ('Ex. 1011', 'Pet. 58-59', 'PO Resp. 30', 'Greenspun Decl. ¶ 56') are part of the doctrinal move and SHOULD be kept inside signal_text when they are integral to the move. A bare standalone citation with no surrounding reasoning is NOT a signal on its own. signal_text 10-300 char window includes citation and exhibit refs when natural.

(e) PTAB AUTHORITY HIERARCHY: the Board is bound by Federal Circuit precedent on patent law (including KSR via the Supreme Court binding through the Federal Circuit), by Supreme Court precedent (KSR, Phillips, Alice, Mayo, etc.), and by its own PRECEDENTIAL opinions (designated by the Director). Other PTAB decisions are non-precedential. When the FWD explicitly notes a precedential vs informative vs routine designation, or 'we are bound by…', the signal evidencing the 'precedent-hierarchy / binding-authority' norm should include that hierarchical marker in signal_text.

(f) Bare procedural recitations (caption, panel list of APJs, banner with case number and patent number, party-counsel list, exhibit list, procedural-history block listing institution date and oral hearing date) emit ZERO signals. Skip the BACKGROUND section unless it contains a doctrinal move (e.g. the Board characterizing the prior-art landscape as a doctrinal move). The CLAIM CONSTRUCTION, ANALYSIS / PATENTABILITY DETERMINATIONS, and CONCLUSION sections are where most signals live.

(g) PRESERVE the source text VERBATIM in passage_text and signal_text. PTAB FWDs often contain artifacts of PDF/OCR conversion: stray newlines mid-sentence, page-number stamps (e.g. 'IPR2014-00305\nPatent 7,062,831 B2\n   \n27'), section symbols (§§), em dashes (—), paragraph symbols (¶, ¶¶), curly quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), footnote markers as small superscripts (3, 5), and occasional OCR errors ('Id.' versus 'Jd.'). Copy character-for-character. Do not normalize, do not correct.

(h) When two or more discrete doctrinal moves appear in the same paragraph (e.g. the Board first states the obviousness standard, then describes the Petitioner's combination, then evaluates the motivation-to-combine, then evaluates the reasonable-expectation-of-success), emit each as its own signal inside the same passage. 4-12 signals per substantive passage is typical for PTAB FWD analysis paragraphs. Norm density is HIGH.
